message.text:
Tracing the browser request for a profile image through each hop to the stored data layer.

The trace covers six hops. The browser requests `GET /file/users/{identifier}/avatar`. The route registers as `GET /users/:identifier/avatar` and maps to `serveUserAvatar`. That function calls `getUserByUsername`, which invokes `Store.GetUser`. The store then calls `ListUsers`, and the driver executes a SQL `SELECT avatar_url FROM user`. An optional authentication hop may occur via `getCurrentUser` on private instances.

The concrete file paths are now mapped. `RegisterRoutes` and `serveUserAvatar` live in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`. `Store.GetUser` and `Store.ListUsers` are in `store/user.go`. The driver SQL runs in `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (or the equivalent MySQL/PostgreSQL file). The avatar data is stored as a base64 data URI inside the `avatar_url` column.

`Store.GetUser` does not cache by username, so it always delegates to `ListUsers`. The avatar data is read from the `avatar_url` column in memory after the database fetch. A separate `GetUserAvatar` RPC path was noted but appears to follow the same route.

GetUserAvatar appears only in ACL configuration, suggesting it may not yet be implemented.

The browser requests profile images through the /file/ route. Server wiring for the fileserver needs verification.

I will trace the profile image request through each hop to the data layer, listing symbols and file paths line by line.

Store.GetUser — store/user.go

The browser request originates from `convertUserFromStore`, which sets the avatar URL to `/file/users/{username}/avatar`. Authentication is skipped because it does not belong to the data retrieval path. The trace stays focused on the data path itself.

The store uses a driver interface. Concrete implementations live in store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/user.go.

RegisterRoutes is the first hop. The avatar URL is `/file/users/{username}/avatar`. The trace will use sqlite as the SQL example.

h07.

Serving handler: **`FileServerService.serveUserAvatar`** — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`

The browser loads `/file/users/{username}/avatar` (set in API responses by `convertUserFromStore` at ```36:36:server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go```). Trace from that GET to stored data:

```
FileServerService.RegisterRoutes — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
Store.GetUser — store/user.go
Store.ListUsers — store/user.go
driver.ListUsers (e.g. (*sqlite.DB).ListUsers) — store/db/sqlite/user.go
SQL SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user — store/db/sqlite/user.go
FileServerService.parseDataURI — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
```

**Notes:**
- Route registration: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` is wired in ```121:124:server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go``` and mounted at startup in ```81:82:server/server.go```.
- `getUserByUsername` calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})` at ```715:716:server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go```.
- `Store.GetUser` delegates to `ListUsers` when there is no ID cache hit (```148:168:store/user.go```).
- The driver runs a `SELECT` including `avatar_url` (```151:164:store/db/sqlite/user.go```; same pattern in `store/db/mysql/user.go` and `store/db/postgres/user.go`).
- Avatars are stored as a base64 data URI in the `user.avatar_url` column; `parseDataURI` decodes it before `c.Blob` returns the image (```196:209:server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go```).
- On private instances, `serveUserAvatar` may call `getCurrentUser` first for auth (```173:180:server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go```), but the target user’s avatar data still comes through the hops above.
